text:
tess: Quick postmortem note from the midnight load run: we observed repeated prefix rehydrates tied to interleaved prefills and eviction sweeps.
anya: I pulled logs. Pattern: prefill starts -> allocs succeed for 1-2 batches -> eviction sweeps reclaim the slab mid-prefill -> prefill retries -> rehydrate later.
kevin: We trimmed prefill backpressure to reduce cold-start latency, but that makes prefill more likely to grab multiple slabs quickly. Combined with aggressive eviction sweep this races.
samir: Two ideas: (A) conservative protection flag during active prefill (with watchdog + TTL), (B) per-prefix eviction-penalty score bump when prefill completes (anti-thrash).
tess: For a short canary I'd prefer A: simpler and observable. Key safety: bounded TTL and node-level protected memory cap.
anya: I'll add metrics: kvcache.prefill.inflight{origin,prefix}, kvcache.evict.skipped_protect, kvcache.protected_memory_pct. Need to know origin (hosted/dedicated/private) to see customer impact.
kevin: Impl sketch: prefill sets meta.protect_until = now + min(est_ms, PROTECT_MAX_MS). Evict checks protect_until and skips if set, incrementing evict.skipped_protect. Also add a watchdog thread that cancels stuck prefills after WATCHDOG_MS and clears protect bit.
samir: For fairness long-term we should consider a debt-ledger: each prefill accrues debt proportional to allocation; eviction can reclaim only if debt below threshold. But that's heavier.
morgan: Canary limits: PROTECT_MAX_MS=30000, node_protected_memory_pct=10%. Abort if protected_count/node > 150 for > 2m or mem_used_pct > 82%.
ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout kevin/prefill-protect v2 started at 2025-04-02T00:12Z
anya: I'll watch dashboards and flag regressions. If behave well, we can iterate toward a debt-ledger follow-up.
tess: Also add a small unit test: simulate prefill stall (sleep) and ensure watchdog clears protect and we don't leak.
kevin: Will open PR and include logs/metrics hooks. ETA ~1h.
morgan: Thanks. I've created ticket: kvcache/prefill-guardrails and attached runbook + rollback criteria.
